title: Any recommendations?
hint: Roll: who's asking, what they need and how you answer. Answer with a real place or thing if you know one.

dice.label: WHO'S ASKING?
faces: a new colleague, new in town

dice.label: WHAT DO THEY NEED?
faces: something to do at the weekend

answers.R: Recommend a real one — and give a tip.
answers.W: One you didn't like: say you wouldn't recommend it — and what you'd recommend instead.
answers.D: You don't know one: say what you'd recommend doing.

R.a: Can you recommend a good place for coffee near the office?
R.b: I'd **highly recommend** the little café by the bus stop. I'd **recommend going** before nine, though — after that there's always a huge queue.

W.a: Is the canteen on the ground floor any good?
W.b: Honestly? I **wouldn't recommend** it — the food's always cold. I'd **recommend** the sandwich place across the road **instead**.

D.a: Any recommendations for lunch around here?
D.b: Sorry, I'm new here too. I'd **recommend asking** Anna — she knows every café in the area.

R.a: Can you recommend a good app for learning Spanish?
R.b: I'd **recommend** Brainscape 😉 Oh, and I'd **recommend doing** ten minutes a day — it works better than an hour once a week.

W.a: Is that fitness app everyone's talking about any good?
W.b: Not really. I **wouldn't recommend** it. It looks great, but twelve euros a month is a bit much. I'd **recommend** a free one **instead**.

D.b: I don't really use one, to be honest. I'd **recommend checking** the reviews first — some of them are full of ads.

R.a: Can you recommend a good dentist?
R.b: I'd **highly recommend** mine — she's really gentle. I'd **recommend booking** well in advance, though: she's always booked up.

W.a: Is the hair salon on the corner any good?
W.b: I **wouldn't recommend** it — they cut way too much off. I'd **recommend** the one near the station **instead**.

D.a: Any recommendations for a doctor who speaks English?
D.b: Sorry, I don't know any. I'd **recommend asking** in the neighbourhood chat — someone always knows.

R.a: We've got a free Saturday. What would you recommend?
R.b: The market in the old town is lovely. I'd **recommend going** early, before it gets busy.

W.a: Is the new escape room any good? I keep seeing ads for it.
W.b: Hmm, I **wouldn't recommend** it — it's short and a bit pricey. I'd **recommend** the bowling alley **instead**.

D.b: Not really — I'm usually at home 😅 I'd **recommend checking** what's on at the cinema.

R.a: Seen anything good lately? I need a new series.
R.b: I'd **highly recommend** Ted Lasso — it's really funny. I'd **recommend watching** it with English subtitles, though: they talk quite fast.

W.a: Is that new crime drama any good?
W.b: I **wouldn't recommend** it — it really drags. I'd **recommend** the book it's based on **instead**.

D.a: Can you recommend something to watch on a long flight?
D.b: I'm not really a series person. I'd **recommend downloading** a few episodes before you go, though!

R.a: Can you recommend a good online shop for clothes?
R.b: I'd **recommend** the one my sister uses — returns are free. I'd **recommend checking** the size chart, though: their clothes run a bit small.

W.a: Have you ever ordered from that cheap website with all the ads?
W.b: Once. I **wouldn't recommend** it — my parcel took six weeks to arrive. I'd **recommend** a local shop **instead**.

D.a: Where can I get a good laptop?
D.b: No idea, to be honest. I'd **recommend waiting** for the sales — laptops are often much cheaper then.

items: **Can you recommend a good** [dentist / app]? – посоветуешь?
**Thanks for the heads-up!** – спасибо, что предупредил
**A friend recommended it to me.** – мне посоветовал
**I'd recommend** [the one by the station] **instead**. – лучше…

speaking: Tell your partner about **two things** you tried because someone recommended them. Would you recommend them too? Why / why not?
Which do you trust more: **a friend's recommendation or online reviews**? Tell your partner about a time a recommendation worked out — or didn't. Would you recommend that thing now?
A friend has **one day** in your city. Plan their day: **three things**, from morning to evening — and a tip for each.
**One thing** you'd recommend to everyone in our group — a book, an app, a place. What tip would you give them?
Tell your partner about **two apps** you use every day: what do you use them for? Would you recommend them? One tip for each (I'd recommend turning on…).
**Two things** you'd never recommend to anyone — a place, a product, a film… What would you recommend instead?
